newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds weaker ahead of FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds weaker ahead of FOMC meeting.

text.p: Irish bonds were weaker in thin volumes on Monday as bond markets range-traded ahead of Tuesday's key Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, dealers said.
"It's very quiet -- several markets around Europe are closed, and no-one's keen to do business until they know the outcome of the FOMC meeting," a dealer said.
The market is split as to whether the FOMC will decide to raise U.S interest rates immediately or wait until the next meeting on July 2.
"Although a delay would be positive for the market in the very short term, I don't think there's much doubt that a hike is ahead," a dealer said.
By 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down six pence at 102.14 to yield 5.92 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was down 15 pence at 109.45 to yield 6.49 percent.
Dealers said the spreads on Irish bonds against German Bunds were broadly unchanged from Friday's close at 145 basis points over in the five-year area and 93 over in the 10-year area.
"We're underperfomring against bunds by one or two basis points today," one said.
Looking ahead, dealers said, the Irish market would be focusing on Tuesday's auction by the National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA)of 100 million Irish pounds of the 8.25 percent bond due 2015.
"The market is anticipating that this auction will go very well, attracting plenty of interest, with domestic rather than foreign money dominating," a dealer said.
The release of the business sentiment index for April by Germany's Ifo institute on Thursday would also provide a focus, dealers said.
